text:
anya: Follow-up from the onprem seed mess - proposing a compact operator contract instead of a full redesign. Wanted quick feedback before I draft RFC.

josh: short summary please?

anya: TL;DR: make seeding resumable and eviction-friendly. Key bits: WAL for chunk receipts, temp chunk store + atomic commit, extended eviction grace for seed workloads, tombstone lifecycle + GC exemptions during retry window, and a small verify tool in airgap.

maria: does WAL mean we force fsync on every chunk? worried about perf.

anya: not necessarily fsync per chunk. WAL will be append-only with periodic fsync (e.g., every 1s or N chunks). The idea is to be crash-recoverable, not crash-proof under 0ms. Configurable durability level.

kevin: I like levels: durability: none|sync-on-commit|periodic-sync. default periodic-sync at 1s. put it in config so customers can pick.

lucy: how do we avoid GC nuking partial uploads? current GC cycles remove temp parts quickly and leaves operator confused.

anya: operator will create a tombstone record for a seed session. Tombstone states: ACTIVE -> PAUSED -> RETRYING -> FAILED -> ABORTED -> COMMITTED. GC ignores tombstones until terminal or TTL expired.

josh: show me a short YAML for the operator config we'll expose to customers.

anya: sure:
```yaml
seedController:
  evictionPolicy:
    graceSeconds: 600
    allowCriticalEvict: false
  retry:
    maxAttempts: 6
    maxWindow: 24h
    backoffBaseSeconds: 5
    backoffFactor: 2
  durabilityLevel: periodic-sync
  gc:
    tombstoneTTL: 48h
    partialRetention: 72h
```

maria: partialRetention separate from tombstoneTTL? seems odd. partialRetention is for temp chunks, tombstoneTTL is for the tombstone state. Keep them separate yes.

kevin: operator events: emit seed.status change with fields: seedID, state, lastOffset, resumeETA, pausedReason, pausedCount. Console will consume these.

lucy: migration plan for existing partials? we have a few customers with stuck seeds.

anya: migration outline I'll include in RFC: 1) run a one-off reconcile job that scans nodes for partials and creates tombstones with retry counters set to 0 2) bump GC TTL to keep partials for 72h during rollout 3) provide `operator seed-reconcile --dry-run` and `--apply` 4) customers can run `seed-checksum-verify` locally before forcing resume.

josh: risk: if we extend TTL we'll consume disk for longer. need to surface disk usage estimate and provide a knob to limit total partial bytes per-node.

maria: good point. add `maxPartialBytesPerNode` and a cluster-level quota that triggers emergency eviction only.

kevin: WAL format proposal (simple): each entry newline-delimited JSON: `{"seed_id":"...","offset":12345,"chunk_hash":"abcd","committed":false,"ts":1670000000}` commit record flips committed true for range. Compact by rewriting checkpoints periodically.

lucy: for airgap bundles: include `seed-checksum-verify` (static Go) and `seed-resume` helper that can validate WAL before calling operator resume.

anya: tests: chaos test where disk pressure triggers eviction mid-transfer, node reboot during transfer, repeated small interruptions, and network blackhole for 30s. Also load tests for WAL latency at 100MB/s.

josh: monitoring: add metrics: seed_active_count, seed_paused_count, seed_resume_rate, seed_bytes_partial_total, seed_wal_sync_latency_ms. Alert on paused_ratio > 0.2 or paused_count > 10.

maria: UX - Console should show per-seed: progress %, lastOffset, resumeETA, pausedReason and action buttons: resume, force-abort (with audit), download-wal, verify-checksum.

kevin: security: ensure temp chunk store permissions restrict other pods. For airgap, signed manifests + chunk hashes must be validated before commit. Operator verifies signature chain.

anya: agrees. also add signed tombstone attestations so operator can't be tricked into committing bogus partials by a compromised node.

ops-bot: note: created issue infra/seed-resume-rfc #278 (https://git.redwood/infra/seed-resume-rfc) and assigned to @anya.

anya: action items I'll include in RFC and tracker: 1) operator API contract doc (state machine + events) 2) WAL + temp store implementation (Go) 3) console events + UI mocks 4) test harness and chaos scenarios 5) airgap bundle tooling (verify + resume) 6) reconciler migrator job 7) documentation + runbook. will propose timeline (3 sprints) and followups for enterprise opt-ins.

josh: please add the migration job as opt-in for first rollout. we need to avoid surprise disk usage.

maria: I'll review the RFC and add test cases. Thanks, this looks actionable.

kevin: thanks all. small ask: add a simple state diagram to the RFC, it helps non-eng folks.

anya: will do. drafting now, pinging when linked.
